articles.title: Number 83 Bus Services Cancelled Due to High Temperatures
articles.excerpt: The number 83 bus services will be cancelled until after 9pm this evening due to operational issues caused by high temperatures, with ticket acceptance on tram services available for affected passengers.
articles.content_html:
The number 83 bus services in Rochdale have been cancelled until after 9pm this evening due to operational issues caused by high temperatures. The cancellation affects all scheduled services on this route, which is a key transport link for many local residents.

In response to the disruption, ticket acceptance has been arranged on tram services along the Rochdale via Oldham line. This measure aims to assist passengers in continuing their journeys despite the bus cancellations.

Passengers are advised to check for updates regarding the resumption of the number 83 services and to plan their journeys accordingly. The situation will be monitored, and further announcements will be made as necessary.

For those affected, it is recommended to use the tram services as an alternative until the bus services are restored.

articles.title: Murder Investigation Launched After Death of 31-Year-Old Nathan Haigh in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: A murder investigation is underway following the death of Nathan Haigh, 31, who was found unresponsive at a flat on Great Howarth. A 37-year-old woman has been arrested on suspicion of murder.
articles.content_html:
BREAKING NEWS — LIVE

Live updates, newest first.

13:33, 13 August 2026

A murder investigation is underway following the death of Nathan Haigh, 31, who was found unresponsive at a flat on Great Howarth. A 37-year-old woman has been arrested on suspicion of murder.

A murder investigation has been launched following the death of a 31-year-old man in Rochdale. Nathan Haigh was found unresponsive at a flat on Great Howarth, near Wardle, shortly before 7.40pm on Tuesday, August 11. Despite the efforts of emergency services, he was pronounced dead at the scene shortly thereafter.

A 37-year-old woman has been arrested on suspicion of murder and remains in custody for questioning. Greater Manchester Police stated that detectives are exploring several lines of enquiry in what they describe as suspicious circumstances. They have reassured the public that there is no wider risk to the community.

Detective Inspector Georgina Fearn from Rochdale CID expressed condolences to Mr Haigh's family and confirmed that specialist officers are available to support them during this difficult time. A police presence remains at the scene, with officers guarding the entrance to the block of flats where the incident occurred. Forensic teams have also been seen examining the property as part of the investigation.

The man's next of kin has been informed, and an inquest is expected to open in due course. Anyone with information related to the investigation is encouraged to contact Greater Manchester Police, quoting log 3306 of August 11.

articles.title: Lift Out of Service at Derker Tram Stop
articles.excerpt: The lift at Derker tram stop is currently out of service, affecting access for passengers. Alternative step-free routes are available for travel towards and away from Manchester.
articles.content_html:
The lift at Derker tram stop is out of service as of 12 August 2026, and will remain unavailable until further notice. This disruption affects passengers using the tram service in both directions.

For those travelling towards Manchester, step-free access is available via a ramp from Cromford Street directly to the Manchester-bound platform. Passengers heading away from Manchester can also use a ramp from Cromford Street, but must cross the tracks to reach the Rochdale-bound platform.

Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has issued an apology for any inconvenience this may cause to commuters and advises passengers to plan their journeys accordingly.

Further updates regarding the lift's status will be provided as they become available. For more information, visit the TfGM travel alerts page.

articles.title: Action Together Achieves Volunteer Centre Quality Accreditation in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Action Together has been awarded the Volunteer Centre Quality Accreditation (VCQA) for the first time in Rochdale, recognising its commitment to volunteering and community support.
articles.content_html:
Action Together has announced that it has achieved the Volunteer Centre Quality Accreditation (VCQA) for the first time in Rochdale. This accreditation, awarded by the National Association for Voluntary and Community Action (NAVCA), highlights the organisation's dedication to supporting volunteers and enhancing community engagement.

The VCQA is a re-accreditation for Action Together in Oldham and Tameside but marks a significant milestone for its operations in Rochdale. The organisation's Volunteering Team, alongside support from the wider Action Together team, worked diligently over several months to meet the accreditation criteria, which include good practice development and the strategic development of volunteering.

Feedback from the assessment praised Action Together for its visibility in the community, high-quality training and development support, and its ability to respond flexibly to the needs of volunteers and local organisations. Comments from partner organisations highlighted Action Together's integral role in the local voluntary sector, noting that it is well embedded in the community and actively participates in local networks.

With this accreditation, Action Together continues to be recognised as the Volunteer Centre for Oldham, Rochdale, and Tameside. The organisation aims to build on this achievement to further enhance its volunteering initiatives and community support services in the region.

articles.title: Rochdale AFC Netball launched as Rochdale Netball Club joins Dale family
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Netball Club is becoming Rochdale AFC Netball in a new partnership with Rochdale AFC and its Community Trust, bringing nearly 200 weekly players into the club's wider sporting family.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Netball Club is joining the Rochdale AFC family under a new identity as Rochdale AFC Netball, in a partnership designed to grow the sport and create more opportunities for women, girls and the wider community across the borough.

The agreement brings together Rochdale AFC, Rochdale AFC Community Trust and one of the borough's established community sports clubs under the wider 'Our Teams' banner.

Rochdale Netball Club currently runs teams from under-six level through to seniors, with nearly 200 players taking to the court each week. Under the new Rochdale AFC Netball identity, the organisations hope to strengthen the route from school participation into junior and adult club netball while also expanding opportunities in coaching, volunteering and leadership.

The partnership is expected to support new programmes in schools, holiday provision, health and wellbeing and volunteer development. The shared Rochdale AFC identity could also open up additional opportunities for sponsorship, commercial support, community events and promotion through the football club.

Amy Williams, Chair of Rochdale AFC Netball, described the move as a fantastic opportunity for both the club and the sport locally, saying joining the Rochdale AFC family would provide a stronger platform to grow the game and inspire more women and girls to become involved.

Rochdale AFC chief executive Laura Thomas, herself a former netball player, said she was thrilled to welcome the club into the wider Rochdale AFC family and stressed that the club's ambition to build a thriving community extends beyond football.

Ryan Bradley, Community Director at Rochdale AFC Community Trust, said the football club, charity and netball club shared common values and could combine their respective strengths. He said bringing the organisations together under one brand would raise netball's profile in Rochdale and strengthen support for volunteers, coaches, community outreach and school work.

Rochdale AFC Netball will be based at Edgar Wood. The Community Trust also pointed to plans for the Community Football and Wellbeing Hub at Bowlee, saying the geographical proximity of the projects made closer cooperation a natural step.

The move follows a wider trend in British sport in which professional football and rugby clubs have partnered with netball organisations to increase visibility, participation and long-term sustainability. In Rochdale, the organisations say their approach will remain community focused and open to people of all ages.

Further information about Rochdale AFC Netball teams, programmes and opportunities to get involved is expected to be announced in due course.

articles.title: Burnley Man Banned from Keeping Animals After Dog Found Emaciated in Rochdale Home
articles.excerpt: A man has received a 15-year ban on keeping animals after an emaciated dog was discovered in a Rochdale property. Paul Lewis Dawson was sentenced at Tameside Magistrates' Court for animal welfare offences.
articles.content_html:
A man has been banned from keeping animals for 15 years after an emaciated dog was found living in unsanitary conditions at a property in Rochdale. Paul Lewis Dawson, 37, of Brownside Road in Burnley, pleaded guilty to three offences under the Animal Welfare Act 2006 at Tameside Magistrates' Court on 31 July.

The RSPCA began investigating on 6 August 2025 after receiving reports about a bullbreed dog named Kano being left unattended at a property on Alice Street in Rochdale. RSPCA inspector Beth Fazackerley and animal rescue officer Francesca Iraci attended the address, where they observed Kano through the keyhole and noted he appeared very skinny. After no one answered the door, they pushed wet dog food through the letterbox, which Kano ate.

Later that evening, the RSPCA returned with a police officer after obtaining a warrant. Upon entering the property, Kano was found to be in poor condition, having difficulty standing and displaying visible signs of distress. The dog was covered in fleas, had wounds on his body, and was suffering from severe weight loss and anaemia due to an insufficient diet. Rubbish and faeces were found throughout the property, creating an unsuitable living environment for the animal.

Dawson received a 22-week prison sentence, suspended for 12 months, and was ordered to complete 18 Rehabilitation Activity Requirement days and 80 hours of unpaid work, in addition to paying £400 in costs. The judge described the case as "the most serious case of animal cruelty I have ever dealt with." Kano has since been taken into the care of the RSPCA and has recovered.
